skill.name: fit-scorer
skill.description: Use when the user asks to "score this influencer", "rank these creators for our campaign", or "tell me which influencer is the best fit"; produces weighted fit scores across audience match, content quality, brand alignment, engagement authenticity, and partnership potential, plus a ranked comparison and a go/pass verdict. Not for finding new influencers — use influencer-discovery; not for sending outreach — use outreach-manager.
skill.summary: Scores shortlisted influencers with weighted audience, content, brand, engagement, and partnership criteria.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, static repository links, metadata URLs, and fixed memory paths. One confirmed issue remains: the skill tells agents to run a local YouTube connector with a user-supplied handle, so handle validation and execution confirmation are needed. No prompt injection, social engineering, or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Connector command execution lacks explicit argument-safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before running the YouTube connector, validate handles as platform handles, and pass arguments without shell interpolation.
State that creator handles must be slug-normalized before reading or writing memory/creators records.

remediation.issue: The API key reference could be misread as a required secret.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that YOUTUBE_API_KEY is optional, user-provided, and never printed or saved in reports.

content.value_statement: Shortlists often rely on subjective opinions and uneven data. This skill applies a weighted scoring framework to rank creators and explain go, consider, or pass decisions.
actual_capabilities: Defines campaign-specific weights across audience, content, brand alignment, engagement quality, and partnership potential.
Scores each shortlisted creator on a 1 to 5 scale with evidence-based notes.
Applies C3 ACE veto checks for follower quality, brand safety, and engagement authenticity.
Builds a ranked comparison for multiple creators with verdicts and key concerns.
Saves a fit-score report path and promotes top picks for downstream planning.
Uses optional YouTube connector data when a measured source is available.
limitations: It does not discover new creators from scratch.
It depends on the quality of metrics, screenshots, or connector data supplied by the user.
It does not send outreach or manage contracts.
It cannot guarantee future campaign performance.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a creator shortlist
use_cases.description: Rank shortlisted influencers before outreach so the team spends time on the strongest fits.

use_cases.title: Standardize agency recommendations
use_cases.description: Compare creators across niches with one rubric and a clear explanation for each recommendation.

use_cases.title: Defend partnership decisions
use_cases.description: Show stakeholders why one creator is safer, stronger, or less suitable than another.

prompt_templates.title: Score one creator
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single candidate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score @handle for my brand. Use this campaign goal and target audience. Tell me whether to pursue, consider, or pass.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare @creator1, @creator2, and @creator3 for this campaign. Rank them and explain the main reason for each verdict.

prompt_templates.title: Use custom weights
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a specific campaign goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these creators for a conversion campaign. Weight audience match at 35 percent and brand alignment at 20 percent.

prompt_templates.title: Audit evidence quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for high-risk partner selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the fit scorer to this shortlist. Use C3 ACE veto checks. Flag weak evidence, assumptions, and data needed before outreach.

output_examples.input: An agency compares three food creators for a restaurant launch.
output: @citybites ranks first because local audience match and comment quality are strongest.
@quickplates is a backup option. @trendfork passes due to weak location fit.

output_examples.input: A brand has limited audience data for a YouTube creator.
output: The report separates measured engagement from assumptions.
It requests missing audience location data before making a final recommendation.

best_practices: Use the same weights for every creator in the same campaign.
Separate measured data from estimates, screenshots, and assumptions.
Run veto checks before ranking so unsafe creators do not score as acceptable.
anti_patterns: Do not use follower count as the primary decision metric.
Do not compare creators across campaigns with different goals without changing weights.
Do not treat a high score as approval when brand safety evidence is missing.

faq.question: Does this skill find influencers?
faq.answer: No. It scores a shortlist you already have. Use influencer discovery first when the list is empty.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare creators across platforms when metrics are normalized and assumptions are stated.

faq.question: Does it require live data connectors?
faq.answer: No. It works with user-supplied inputs. Connectors can improve metric quality when available.

faq.question: What scoring scale does it use?
faq.answer: It uses a 1 to 5 scale and weighted dimensions that can change by campaign goal.

faq.question: How does it handle fake engagement?
faq.answer: It applies engagement authenticity checks and C3 ACE veto rules when evidence shows bought or coordinated engagement.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
